lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - Talk about the pictures. Make predictions.

details: Talk about the pictures activates prior knowledge and sets the scene. Students describe the different environments (city vs. countryside) and the transport they see to predict what the children will encounter.
Look for simple descriptions like "city," "bus," "trees," or "bike" and pointing to the characters walking.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - Listen to the story.

details: Listen to the story develops narrative comprehension. Students listen to the first part of the story to understand the repeating pattern "I walk to school. What can I see?" and identifying the answers.
Look for attentive listening and pointing to trace the story as it progresses.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - Act it out.

details: Act it out builds confidence and fluency. Students role-play the characters, walking on the spot and mime looking around, then saying "I can see..."
Look for clear delivery of the key phrase "What can I see?" and the appropriate waving action to the imaginary bus or bike.

lessonPlan.topic: Numbers Book p107 - Continue the pattern. Draw and colour.

details: Continue the pattern develops logical reasoning. Students identify the repeating sequence of shape and colour (e.g., Red Triangle, Green Square) and draw the next items in the row.
Look for correct identification of the pattern rules (AB, AB...) and drawing the correct shape in the correct colour to finish the line.

lessonPlan.topic: Numbers Book p108 - Trace and say.

details: Trace and say reinforces spelling and pronunciation. Students trace the number words to practise writing the complex numbers.
Look for neat tracing of the hyphenated number words (e.g., "sixty-four").
